market_wrap.text: Nifty fell 1.75% to 25,350 (Sensex −1,484 points) after a gap-up open reversed into broad selling. Profit-taking after a strong November rally, a roughly 93% market-implied chance of a December US Fed rate rise, a rupee near 93 per dollar and the global AI-stock sell-off weighed; banks and metals led the fall, with Tata Steel down about 8.5% on its APL Apollo deal, while IT stocks rose.

reasons.reason: These are Friday 20 November NAVs (today's had not been published by about 10 pm IST); they reflect Friday's slump in silver, which capped bullion's steepest weekly fall in eight months on a strong dollar and bets on a December US Fed rate rise. Silver bounced about 3% on Monday from its lowest level since September 2025.

No company news found today. Steel and metal stocks were the day's worst sector (Nifty Metal −3.7%) as Tata Steel slumped about 8% on its ₹28,000 crore tubes-business sale and APL Apollo stake purchase, and BLEL closed at a fresh 52-week low.

No company news found today. Indian AI-linked stocks including Netweb fell as the global AI sell-off deepened after the Nasdaq dropped over 5% on Friday; Indian IT services stocks rose, but Netweb trades with the AI-hardware theme rather than with them.

news.headline: Gold and silver rebound 2–3% after last week's crash
news.summary: Spot gold rose about 2% and silver about 3% on Monday as the dollar and crude eased, after last week's steepest weekly fall in eight months; a December Fed rate rise is still about 97% priced and US PCE inflation data is due this week.

news.headline: Happiest Minds hits 52-week low after eight straight falls
news.summary: The stock touched ₹291.15, down about 8% over eight sessions and about 41% over a year; the report notes higher debt and interest costs in the half-year and promoter pledging of about 25%.

outlook.view: Gold and silver bounced 2–3% on 23 November from their lowest levels since September 2025 after the steepest weekly fall in eight months; the dollar near 104 and a roughly 97%-priced December US rate rise still weigh on bullion.
outlook.watch: US PCE inflation (25 Nov) and the 8–9 December Fed decision.

outlook.view: A global sell-off in AI stocks hit Asian hardware names today (Taiwan −6.2%, Korea over 5%), weighing on AI-server maker Netweb, while Indian IT services stocks rose (Nifty IT +1.3%).
Record copper prices drove Hindustan Copper's profit surge, but copper has since slipped to a five-month low on a strong dollar and weak China data, dragging metal stocks.
